title: trailboss --json start
description: One row: the agent `start` would start (no --yes), or started (--yes), from an agent definition, in a new host terminal in a folder, outside a task: no worktree, no branch. The command runs directly, never through a shell. Started, its label is kept so `live` and `resume` show it. A start that fails is an error, not a row. Frontends should show an action they don't know as is.

action.description: would start or started; more may be added.

definition.description: The definition's name, as `agents ls` lists it.

kind.description: claude, codex, gemini, copilot, opencode or pi.

path.description: The definition's file; null for a built-in one.

trust.description: A repository definition's trust: always trusted here (an untrusted one is refused). Null for yours and built-in ones.

argv.description: What it runs, with the first prompt (the definition's rules and the brief) shown as `<brief>`; without a brief, the definition's rules alone, else no prompt at all.

command.description: argv as one line to read; nothing runs it through a shell.

brief.description: Whether it was given a first prompt (--task or --task-file). The brief itself isn't printed.

label.description: --name, else the definition's name: its terminal's name, and what `live` and `resume` show.

host.description: herdr, tmux, …; null when no host is running (the plan then says so).

terminal.description: The new terminal's address, once started.

parent.description: AGENT:ID of the session it belongs to: the one named with --parent, else the one it was started from.
